notes: Pinned by docs/devel/implementation/contracts/dependencies.json (filc 0.685) and installed per task F00. Both x86_64 assets downloaded from the v0.685 GitHub release and verified byte-for-byte (size and sha256) against the digests published in the release API metadata (https://api.github.com/repos/pizlonator/fil-c/releases/tags/v0.685). Release note names: the pizfix tarball is the self-contained musl distribution (compiler only, no root); optfil is the glibc /opt/fil distribution (compiler plus many programs; its setup.sh requires root). There is no executable named filc or optfil in either distribution: the actual compiler names are build/bin/clang and build/bin/filcc (pizfix; symlinks to clang-20) and /opt/fil/bin/filcc and fil++ (optfil; symlinks to filcc-clang-20). Canonical recipe: no extra flags are required; the driver adds -lpizlo/-lyolort/-lyoloc/-lyolom/-lyolounwind and the Fil-C CRT objects automatically and produces a dynamically linked PIE (pizfix interpreter <root>/pizfix/lib/ld-fil1-x86_64.so with RUNPATH to pizfix/lib, NEEDED libc.so/libpizlo.so/libyoloc.so; optfil interpreter /opt/fil/lib/ld-fil1-x86_64.so, NEEDED libc.so.6666/libpizlo.so/libyolocimpl.so/libyolomimpl.so). It is not a static-link toolchain. The shared application flag set -std=c11 -D_POSIX_C_SOURCE=200809L -D_GNU_SOURCE -Wall -Wextra -Werror -pthread -O2 -g also compiles and runs 'Hello from Fil-C!' with both compilers (exit 0). optfil relocation: because the shipped filcc-clang-20 resolves its own executable path and only uses /opt/fil/{include,lib} when that path is under the literal /opt/fil prefix, a /opt/fil symlink to the local tree makes it fall back to system paths and link with /usr/lib/Scrt1.o etc. (fails: cannot find /usr/lib/Scrt1.o, filc_crt.o, -lc, -lpizlo). The physical tree is therefore kept at /home/msaraiva/.local/fil-c/0.685/optfil-0.685-linux-x86_64/opt/fil and bind-mounted at /opt/fil (sudo mount --bind); the unmodified shipped binaries then report the ld line -dynamic-linker /opt/fil/lib/ld-fil1-x86_64.so ... -L/opt/fil/lib and compile/run hello correctly. This mount is runtime state (does not survive reboot; vendor/scripts/filc.sh recreates it). Alternative canonical install if the integrator prefers a persistent /opt/fil: cd <optfil unpack dir> && sudo ./setup.sh -u (extracts fil.tar.xz directly to /opt/fil; optional SSH/system configuration declined).
